priceNote: Live $0.87 (+1.16%) on Nov 4, 2026 — down ~6% from $0.93 at the Aug 4 report, near the $0.76 52-week low (high $3.31); 52-week range $0.76-$3.31. Nov 4 tape: S&P futures -1.2% / Nasdaq -2% on a Democratic midterm sweep; Dec 9 hike ~85% priced.
summary: REFRESH (prior report Aug 4, 2026): no new company news since the Q2 update. Onvansertib's data are strong (CRDF-004 30 mg arm: 72% ORR vs 43% pooled SoC, PFS HR 0.37, ASCO Jun 2026) and support a registrational program, but the Phase 3 start is pushed to 2027 and the Nerviano license dispute is unresolved. ⚠️ SURVIVAL: cash funds operations only into Q1 2027 — a raise before Phase 3 is near-certain. Kept as a carryover only because the data quality is real and ~$60M prices in heavy dilution. Base cut from +45% to +35% (above the lane's realized 30d P75 (+12.2%; written-Base bias +72.7pp)), assuming a partnering or financing that resolves the Nerviano dispute within ~3-6 months. แนะนำ 1% ของ portfolio เท่านั้น — ถ้า thesis fail ลงได้ 70%+.

risks: ⚠️ SURVIVAL: Cash is guided to fund operations only into Q1 2027 (~8 months of runway from Aug 2026) even after the Jul 2026 $10M raise, and the newly-detailed CRDF-005 Phase 3 trial will require $128–192M — more than double Cardiff's entire ~$64M market cap. Another dilutive raise is all but certain, and it will likely need to be far larger than July's.

⚠️ SURVIVAL: The Jul 15, 2026 registered direct offering priced at $1.05 triggered a -32.1% single-day decline, and the stock (now $0.93) still trades below that raise price — recent institutional buyers are underwater, a real signal of weak capital-markets access ahead of the next, larger raise this company will need.

The Nerviano license dispute remains unresolved 10+ weeks after Cardiff sued (May 19, 2026) and Nerviano issued its termination notice (May 27, 2026) — no court ruling or settlement has been reported as of Aug 2026; if Nerviano ultimately prevails, Cardiff loses its only clinical asset outright, regardless of trial data quality.

Phase 3 initiation guidance has slipped from 'H2 2026' (as of the Jul 22 report) to 2027 — a full year+ push-out — and analysts have already cut probability-of-success assumptions from 60% to 50%, specifically citing the licensing overhang.

Nano-cap ($63.9M) with extreme volatility (52-week range $0.7566–$3.31, a 4.4x spread) and a fresh 52-week low set since the last report — thin liquidity and wide spreads are a real execution risk on top of the fundamental risks above.

macroRisk.sectorImpact: CRDF's litigation and clinical catalysts are idiosyncratic and macro-independent, but the financing overlay compounds directly in a high-rate environment — with a $128-192M Phase 3 funding need against a $64M market cap, every basis point of rate matters to how dilutive the next raise (likely equity, given the going-concern flag) will be.

catalystSpot.preRunup: Clinical-stage nano-caps with pending litigation or license risk typically trade heavy and range-bound rather than running up ahead of resolution — CRDF's own muted +2.03% reaction to genuinely strong Phase 2 data (Jun 2, 2026) shows the license overhang dominating sentiment over the science, and that pattern has persisted through Aug 2026 with no resolution.

catalystSpot.preRunupPct: 0% to +10% pre-event drift; frequently flat-to-negative given the license overhang and now-quantified financing gap

postLose.note: CRDF's own Jul 15-16, 2026 dilutive $10M registered direct offering at $1.05 triggered a -32.11% single-day decline — a direct, sourced example of how the market punishes financing-driven negative catalysts on this stock specifically, and the template for how a bad litigation ruling or forced next raise would likely trade.
